To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the clinical effectiveness of telemedicine is high, the economic impact of this technology is positive, and the organizational impact is limited.

(i) telemedicine applications can provide clinical benefits; (ii) telemedicine applications are not necessarily more costly than the traditional ones; (iii) the economic benefits of telemedicine applications depend on the organizational context in which they are implemented.

'telemonitored polysomography is an effective technology, provided that the clinical trial is carefully designed to take account of all technical conditions and the clinical results are interpreted accordingly.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an evaluation process that is able to provide a better understanding of the real effects of telemedicine.
the following question: what can we learn from the early clinical assessment of a telemedicine application in order to conduct a more comprehensive economic evaluation?
the development of a methodology for early evaluation of telemedicine and the production of relevant data for the economic evaluation of this technology.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the slow diffusion of telehealth applications is mainly due to the lack of a medical and economic evaluation of telehealth applications.
the slow development of telemedicine is not due to the lack of technical effectiveness, but rather to the lack of a comprehensive evaluation process.

telemedicine is not a'magic' tool, but a useful technology, whose diffusion should be carefully planned, taking into account its clinical and economic effectiveness, and its impact on the organization of care.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
telemonitored polysommnography is a reliable, efficient and cost-effective technology.

the medical community should be involved at an early stage of the development of telemedicine, not only to ensure the quality of the technology but also to provide the data that will be used in economic evaluations.

the clinical evaluation of telemedicine can be conducted as any other evaluation of medical technology, and it is not necessarily a priori more difficult to assess the effectiveness of a new technology than that of a new medical drug.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the medical community has to be involved in the early stages of the development process of telemedicine in order to ensure that it is not used as a substitute for the traditional medical practice.
, in order to promote a better diffusion of telemedicine, one should first of all focus on clinical evaluation and, in a second step, economic evaluation.

, in order to promote telemedicine, the medical community should be provided with a set of tools that would enable them to assess telemedicine and to produce convincing arguments in favor of the technology.
